title: Brand deal pricing request
description: What one pricing run is given. Two separations are load-bearing. First, a term the brief never mentioned is 'unspecified', never a default: the omissions are the product, because a fee quoted before usage rights and exclusivity are settled is quoting for a scope nobody has agreed. Second, every account figure carries how it was obtained, so a number the creator typed can be told apart from one that was retrieved.

assessed_at.description: The date the run is made. Framework staleness is measured against this, not against the machine clock.

framework_version.description: Pin a specific pricing framework version. Null takes whatever version the package ships.

mode.description: quote: the creator needs a number to send. review: a brief arrived and needs decomposing. counter: an offer is on the table and needs answering.

marketplace_comparables.description: Optional. Asking prices observed on public creator-marketplace profiles for accounts comparable to this one. No connector supplies these; they are gathered only where a caller can browse the public web and the site permits it, and a run without them is complete.

brand_ad_evidence.description: Optional. What advertising this brand is currently running. It is context for the negotiation - a brand with a standing ad budget is a different conversation from one running nothing - and it is never evidence of what they will pay a creator. It must not move a price, and the pricing engine is built so that it cannot.

income_breakdown.description: True when the ask is what the creator's income adds up to. The quote then also prints its income rows as the brand-deal part of that breakdown; platform payouts stay with the platform-monetization Skill.

stated_budget.description: What the brand said they would pay, if they said anything. Recorded to be compared against, never used as the answer.

format.description: Production cost and shelf life both follow the format, so it prices separately from the platform.

terms.description: Six terms decide most of the final number. Each one is either specified in the brief or is not; 'unspecified' is the honest default and becomes a question rather than an assumption.

status.description: none_granted when the brief explicitly grants no reuse, no paid use and no buyout. It is a settled term, not a zero-day licence; leave the licence fields empty or false.

paid_amplification.description: Whether the brand will run the content as a paid ad. Priced apart from the licence duration because it is a different question.

account_facts.description: Account evidence, used to place a tier and to decide two premiums. Precision matters far less here than in an eligibility check: a few percent either way does not change which band applies.

niche.description: Free text. Only matches against the niche premium and the reach model when it names one of the niches those carry.

audience_geography.description: Unknown leaves the geography premium out rather than guessing which way it would move.

brand_ad_evidence.description: A projection of one advertising-activity lookup. Deliberately carries no budget figure: the source can show what a brand advertises, and nothing in it supports a claim about what that brand will spend on a creator.

matched_name.description: Null means nothing matched the name searched, which may only be a spelling difference. That is not the same as a brand that was found and is running nothing.

coverage_complete.description: False when the ad list did not end within the pages the lookup could read, which makes the count a floor rather than a total.

marketplace_comparables.description: Raw observations only. The distribution is computed downstream so that the same listings always produce the same band, and so that a caller cannot hand in a conclusion dressed as evidence.

deliverable_format.description: The deliverable these prices are for. A price for a static post is not evidence about a video.

price.description: The asking price shown on the profile. A listing without a visible price is not an observation.

basis.description: Retrieved means it came back from a lookup. A figure the creator recalled is usable but stays labelled all the way to the report.
